title: Implement a Trie
statement:
Implement a trie, also called a prefix tree: a structure that stores words so you can quickly check for a whole word or for a prefix. Write a class for its nodes and a trie class with three operations:

- `insert word` stores `word`.
- `search word` returns `true` when `word` was inserted, and `false` otherwise.
- `startsWith prefix` returns `true` when at least one inserted word starts with `prefix`, and `false` otherwise. A word counts as starting with itself.

The trie starts empty. The first line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Words and prefixes are lowercase letters only. Print the answer to each `search` and `startsWith` on its own line.

Input:

```text
6
insert apple
search apple
search app
startsWith app
insert app
search app
```

Expected output:

```text
true
false
true
true
```

tests.stdin:
6
insert apple
search apple
search app
startsWith app
insert app
search app

7
search a
startsWith a
insert car
insert cart
search car
search cart
search ca

6
insert dog
startsWith dog
startsWith dogs
search do
startsWith d
search dog

10
insert tea
insert ten
insert ten
insert inn
search te
startsWith te
search ten
startsWith tex
search inn
startsWith i
tests.output:
false
true
true
false
true
true

tests.stdin:
5
insert a
search a
startsWith a
search b
startsWith ab

hints: Each node stands for one prefix. It holds a child for each letter that can come next, and a flag that says whether a whole word ends there.
To insert, start at the root and go down one letter at a time, making a child when it's missing. Mark the last node as the end of a word.
`search` and `startsWith` go down the same way and fail when a child is missing. They differ only at the end, where `search` also needs the end flag.
